title: Proposition
body_md: If a continuous-time system \eqref{eq:sys_cont} can be transformed into a structurally flat triangular form \eqref{eq:structurally_flat_triangular_form_continuous_time_system} via a state- and input transformation \eqref{eq:trafo_cont}, then the implicit Euler discretization of the system $\dot{\bar{x}}=f(\bar{x}, u)$ is backward-flat according to Definition \ref{def:backward-flatness}.

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Since the input-output behavior of the closed-loop system is given by $y_{[0]}=v$, the new input $v$ directly determines the values of the flat output. Hence, perfect tracking of a desired trajectory $y^d$ could be achieved by choosing $v=y^d$, resulting in error dynamics of order $0$.
        However, as demonstrated in the following, this approach is not suitable for practical applications. We therefore focus instead on the design of tracking control laws for systems of the forms \eqref{eq:Brunovsky_dyn} and \eqref{eq:Brunovsky_red}, with error dynamics of orders $\#R_1$ and $\#\lambda-m$, respectively.
